subject: Pre-QBR: Scaling headroom & unit-cost playbook for GPU ops
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Pre-QBR: Scaling headroom & unit-cost playbook for GPU ops

Team —

As prep for the QBR next week I pulled together a simple headroom matrix and three cost scenarios that map expected GPU spend to utilization, batching/caching levers, and customer SLAs. See attached "gpu_headroom_matrix.xlsx" and the brief PDF. High-level ask: we need to land one prioritized playbook and a decision on reserved vs spot mix for Dedicated pools so the finance slide can lock the run-rate numbers.

Key context (summary):
- Current cluster utilization: ~68% across prod pools (Mar–Apr).
- Batching experiments show 12–22% token-cost improvement depending on mix and latency SLO.
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate varies by workload (20–55%); lifecycle caching can recover another ~6–10% token cost in steady state.

Proposed scenarios in the sheet:
1) Base (conservative): keep current reserved capacity, enable baseline batching heuristics, no new caching rollout.
2) Optimized (recommended): +10% reserved for predictable demand, enable aggressive batching for background requests, rollout prefix cache to 50% of high-volume routes.
3) Growth (risk-tolerant): +25% reserved, more spot instances for burst, experimental quantized variants for non-PLG traffic.

Decisions we need before the QBR:
- Pick scenario or hybrid and provide the expected monthly GPU spend delta.
- Confirm owners for canary (who runs the rollout and the rollback plan).
- Acceptable latency delta thresholds by route (we need these for tradeoff slides).

Ask: please review the attached matrix and reply with the delta numbers you can own by EOD tomorrow so I can bake into the deck. If you prefer a 20–30 min sync instead, say so and I’ll schedule.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Strategy
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Attached the raw experiment outputs (batching_experiment_results.csv) and I pulled the short table into the sheet. Quick operational read:
- Utilization baseline: 68% (prod pools), spike 86% at 11:00 UTC on demo days.
- Batching effect: 12% cost savings for mixed small/large requests at conservative batch windows; up to 22% with a 60–80ms batch window at the expense of P95 latency (about +40–60ms on chat P95).
- Cache impact: enabling prefix/KV cache for the top 20 routes raised hit rate from 28% -> 48% and reduced token generation by ~9% for those routes.

Operational recommendations (short):
- For the Optimized scenario (recommended):
  * Reserved +10% for prod pools to reduce burst reliance on expensive spot and preemptions. Estimated committed monthly spend +$84k.
  * Aggressive batching for background/ingest routes; keep chat/low-latency routes on conservative batching. Expected token-cost reduction ~14% net across traffic.
  * Staged cache rollout (week 1: Canary on non-critical routes, week 2: expand to 50% of high-volume routes).
- For Growth scenario: quantify quantized variants separately — we expect another 6–8% CPU/GPU efficiency but need a 2-week validation window and additional SLOs.

Owners: infra to run canary (marissa_cole), SRE to own rollback playbook (markus_klein), product to sign off on latency deltas (lauren_bishop).

I’ll add committed vs variable breakdown to the sheet and push an updated version by EOD.

Marissa
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
